HiTOP-DAT Norms

Source: R/data.R
hitopdat_norms.Rd

The mean and standard deviation that norm_hitopdat() converts each HiTOP-DAT scale score against, one row per normed scale. The battery's authors named each source in their answers to the package maintainer's questions in 2026, and this table takes each value from the source they named:

Usage

hitopdat_norms

Format

A tibble with 53 rows and 8 columns:

Measure

The measure the scale belongs to, as in hitopdat_scales$Measure

Scale

Name of the scale, as in hitopdat_scales$Scale

camelCase

The name of the scale converted to camel case, as in hitopdat_scales$camelCase

M

The reference sample's mean

SD

The reference sample's standard deviation

Sample

The reference sample, as its source describes it

N

The reference sample's size (integer), where the source prints one. NA for the CAT-PD facets, whose workbook gives none, and for the CAPE, whose source prints the men's and women's n (in Sample) but no total.

Source

Where the mean and SD come from

Details

  • WHODAS: Andrews et al. (2009), Table 1, the total row and total column (N = 8,824).

  • The 18 IDAS-II scales: Watson et al. (2012), Table 2, the "Adults" column (N = 1,091).

  • CAPE positive symptoms: Galletly et al. (2016), Table 1. The mean is the mean of the men's 26.26 (n = 125) and the women's 26.58 (n = 180), weighted by their n, and the SD is the 3.52 printed for both. Both are divided by the 20 items, because score_hitopdat() scores the CAPE as an item mean.

  • The 33 CAT-PD facets: Len Simms's CAT-PD and IDAS scoring workbook, the "Community" mean and SD of its "CAT-PD Scoring" sheet, at the precision the workbook stores. These norms are unpublished. The battery's authors use them, and the package follows the authors.

Each mean and SD is on the metric score_hitopdat() scores the scale on: a sum for the WHODAS and the IDAS-II, and an item mean for the CAPE and the CAT-PD.

The IDAS-II General Depression scale has no row, because the authors dropped it. The AUDIT, DUDIT and PHQ-15 have no row and get no T score. The AUDIT and DUDIT norms are split by sex, and how to report them waits on the authors' answer. The authors keep the PHQ-15 on its cutoff scores rather than a T score.

norm_hitopdat() also flags an IDAS-II Suicidality or CAT-PD Self-Harm T score of 65 or more, the alert point Katherine Jonas gave in her email to the package maintainer of 2026-10-15. She added that clinics may set another, so the function takes it as an argument.

References

Andrews, G., Kemp, A., Sunderland, M., Von Korff, M., & Ustun, T. B. (2009). Normative data for the 12 item WHO Disability Assessment Schedule 2.0. PLoS ONE, 4(12), e8343. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0008343

Galletly, C., Clark, L., McFarlane, A., Searle, A., Sawyer, M., Sim, M., Baghurst, P., & van Hooff, M. (2016). Childhood lead exposure, childhood trauma, substance use and subclinical psychotic experiences: A longitudinal cohort study. Psychiatry Research, 239, 54-61. doi:10.1016/j.psychres.2016.02.066

Simms, L. J. (n.d.). CAT-PD and IDAS scoring [Unpublished Excel workbook]. Received by the package maintainer from K. G. Jonas, 2026-10-15.

Watson, D., O'Hara, M. W., Naragon-Gainey, K., Koffel, E., Chmielewski, M., Kotov, R., Stasik, S. M., & Ruggero, C. J. (2012). Development and validation of new anxiety and bipolar symptom scales for an expanded version of the IDAS (the IDAS-II). Assessment, 19(4), 399-420. doi:10.1177/1073191112449857

See also

norm_hitopdat(), score_hitopdat(), hitopdat_scales
